newsitem.title: USA: U.S. concern over Bosnian spy network - L.A. Times.
newsitem.headline: U.S. concern over Bosnian spy network - L.A. Times.

text.p: The Clinton administration has received a secret report that says Bosnia's Moslem government is setting up an underground intelligence service heavily influenced by Iran, according to U.S. intelligence sources, the Los Angeles Times reported in its Thursday edition.

The paper said the classified intelligence report being circulated throughout the administration said a senior Bosnian government official forced out of power under American pressure in November because of his close ties to Iran was setting up a secret intelligence network for Bosnian President Alija Izetbegovic.

The Times said that according to U.S. sources the report stated that Hasan Cengic -- fired as Bosnia's deputy defence minister after the United States threatened to withhold $100 million in military aid to Bosnia -- has taken on an unofficial but influential intelligence role on behalf of Izetbegovic, an old friend.

The paper said that if the report were entirely accurate Cengic's powerful, unofficial intelligence role would mark a major setback in U.S. eforts to reduce or eliminate Iranian influence in Bosnia, which has remained one of the biggest strategic problems for the Clinton administration in the Balkans since the Dayton peace accords were signed in November 1995.
The paper said the Clinton administration had not yet talked to Izetbegovic about the report.
A cargo vessel with $100 million worth of military equipment for Bosnia sat idling in the Adriatic for a month toward the end of last year, waiting for Sarajevo to remove Cengic.
